'''Edith Conrad Halbert''' (23 April 1931 – 31 December 2023)<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mottmckameyfh.com/obituaries/edith-halbert |title=Edith Conrad Halbert |author=<!--Not stated--> |access-date=26 March 2024}}</ref> was an American physicist, elected a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] in 1972.<ref name=aps>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Fellows nominated in 1972 by the Division of Nuclear Physics|work=APS Fellow Archive|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=1972&unit_id=DNP&institution=|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210109075911/https://aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=1972&unit_id=DNP&institution= |archive-date=2021-01-09 |access-date=2020-08-26|publisher=[[American Physical Society]]|language=en}}</ref> She worked on computations in the [[nuclear shell model]] at the [[Oak Ridge National Laboratory]].

==Education==
Halbert attended [[Cornell University]],<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=The Cornell Daily Sun 30 October 1951|url=https://cdsun.library.cornell.edu/?a=d&d=CDS19511030.1.3&|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2020-08-26|website=cdsun.library.cornell.edu}}</ref> where she was elected to [[Sigma Xi]]<ref>{{cite magazine|magazine=Cornell Alumni News|volume=54|issue=1|date=July 1951|hdl=1813/27580|title=Sigma Xi Elects|page=15}}</ref> and graduated with a bachelor's degree in 1951.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=The Cornell Daily Sun 8 June 1951|url=https://cdsun.library.cornell.edu/cgi-bin/cornell?a=d&d=CDS19510608-01.2.44|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2020-08-26|website=cdsun.library.cornell.edu}}</ref> She then went to the [[University of Rochester]] to pursue graduate studies in physics. At Rochester, she was the student of [[James Bruce French]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Koltun|first=Daniel S.|date=September 2002|title=James Bruce French|journal=Physics Today|language=en|volume=55|issue=9|pages=77–79|doi=10.1063/1.1522227|bibcode=2002PhT....55i..77K|issn=0031-9228|doi-access=free}}</ref> She earned a doctorate in 1957<ref>{{Cite news|last=|first=|date=1957-06-10|title=Degrees Awarded at UR's Commencement|pages=16|work=Democrat and Chronicle|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/31206852/democrat-and-chronicle/|access-date=2020-08-26}}</ref> with a PhD thesis entitled ''A Shell Model for the Even-Parity States of Nitrogen-15''.<ref>{{Cite thesis|last=Halbert|first=Edith C.|title=A Shell Model for the Even-Parity States of Nitrogen-15|date=1957|degree=PhD|publisher=[[University of Rochester]]|bibcode=1957PhDT........21H|url=https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/1957PhDT........21H/abstract}}</ref>

==Career==
She worked at the [[Oak Ridge National Laboratory]],<ref>{{Cite journal|last=|first=|date=April 1964|title=We Hear That|url=http://physicstoday.scitation.org/doi/10.1063/1.3051583|journal=[[Physics Today]]|language=en|volume=17|issue=4|pages=98–100|doi=10.1063/1.3051583|bibcode=1964PhT....17d..98.|issn=0031-9228|via=|url-access=subscription}}</ref> where she directed the development of the Oak Ridge–Rochester Multi-Shell Program, a computer program used to compute the properties of atomic nuclei based on the [[nuclear shell model]].<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=C3fFUYXzKdAC&pg=RA2-PA156|pages=156–160|journal=Oak Ridge National Laboratory Review|title=Nuclear Physics Research: Little Things Mean a Lot|volume=25|issue=3–4|year=1992}}</ref> While at Oak Ridge, she also worked as a visiting scientist in the low energy nuclear theory group at the [[Brookhaven National Laboratory]] and the nuclear theory group at [[Stony Brook University]].<ref>{{cite book|contribution=Domestic assignments and leaves of absence|page=180|url=https://www.osti.gov/servlets/purl/4921301|title=Physics Division Annual Progress Report, Period Ending December 31, 1971|date=May 1972|publisher=Oak Ridge National Laboratory|doi=10.2172/4921301|last1=Obenshain|first1=F. E.|osti=4921301}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Halbert came from a [[Forest Hills, New York]] family. She married Melvyn Halbert of [[Jamaica, New York]], also a Cornell and University of Rochester physics student<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pas.rochester.edu/news-events/newsletter/cross-sections/csWinter02.pdf |title=Cross Sections, Department Of Physics and Astronomy, University of Rochester, Winter 2002}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://cdsun.library.cornell.edu/?a=d&d=CDS19510117-01.2.50& |access-date=2021-02-21 |title=The Cornell Daily Sun 17 January 1951 |website=cdsun.library.cornell.edu}}</ref> and later an Oak Ridge researcher.
